header:
Date: 2027-08-18
Time: 15:30-16:22 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood participants: Maya Chen (AE), Jules Park (SE), Ravi Patel (SE)
Customer participants: Elena Rossi (CTO), Marco Diaz (Sr Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Product), Aaron Lee (SRE), Luis Ortega (Security)
summary: Initial integration discovery for Clearsky evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus on SDK interoperability with LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy pattern, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks, and VPC networking. Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS) are gating items. Agreed next steps: share security docs, sample SDK + LangChain notebook, schedule deep-dive on VPC networking, and provide preliminary Dedicated pricing.
topics: Observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost, per-route metrics)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SAML/SSO, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. We're Maya, Jules and Ravi from Redwood.
[00:06] Elena (Clearsky): Hi Maya, hi team. Happy to be here. We wanted to run through how we could plug Redwood into our stack — specifically SDKs, proxy/gateway ideas, and the VPC story.
[00:15] Maya: Great, quick agenda — intro, current infra and constraints, integration options (hosted/dedicated/private), SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, observability and SLAs, next steps. Is that good?
[00:26] Elena: Yep, sounds right.
[00:28] Marco: Quick note — our load is bursty, mostly daytime US; average qps about 60, spikes to ~350 for 30-45s. P95 latency target is under 300ms for short prompts.
[00:40] Jules (Redwood SE): Cool — that helps. When you say short prompts, token lengths?
[00:44] Marco: Typically 40-120 tokens per request, some longer >512 for few workflows but not common.
[00:52] Maya: Thanks Marco. On the security front? any blockers we should know up front?
[00:56] Luis (Security): SOC2 required, SAML SSO for console access, want KMS-backed key management for any private deployments. Also audit logs with 365 retention preferred.
[01:07] Maya: Totally doable — we have SOC2 docs, SAML, and KMS integrations for Private/Dedicated. We'll send details after.
[01:14] Priya: One question — we use LangChain for our multi-step agents and LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented tasks. How smooth is the SDK integration there?
[01:23] Jules: Good question. Redwood SDKs have first-class support for both. We have examples: LangChain wrapper, LlamaIndex connectors. For hosted we provide direct SDK calls; for Dedicated/Private you get the same endpoint semantics but inside your VPC.
[01:37] Aaron (SRE): Are there client-side proxies or do you recommend a gateway approach? We run a gateway for auth and rate limiting today.
[01:44] Maya: We see two patterns — direct SDK calls from app servers -> Redwood (simpler), or internal gateway/proxy that centralizes auth, quota enforcement, caching. Gateway is handy if you want uniform policy or plan to switch backend models without changing clients.
[01:58] Marco: If we do a gateway, can Redwood's rate limit headers be surfaced? We need to integrate into our existing token bucket system.
[02:05] Jules: Yes — Redwood returns standard headers for remaining quota, usage, and estimated cost. You can also get per-route metrics via our observability hooks and tracing. We'll send the header schema.
[02:16] Elena: What about burst handling — do you do queuing or throttling on Dedicated pools?
[02:21] Jules: Dedicated supports configurable burst capacity and autoscale policies. For spikes like 350 qps short bursts we recommend a small buffer and smart routing; you'll also get predictable tail latency because the pool is isolated. For Hosted we have fallback policies to different regions or model variants but that can add variability.
[02:40] Aaron: Any examples of LangChain usage? We sometimes see tokenization mismatches in integration.
[02:46] Jules: We'll share a notebook. The SDK exposes streaming and chunked output so LangChain's streaming agents work well. Watch out for tokenization differences if you run different tokenizer models locally; we document exact tokenization per model.
[02:58] Marco: On the observability side, we need token-level cost breakdown and per-caller tracing to tie to our cost center. Can Redwood integrate with our Datadog and Jaeger?
[03:08] Ravi: Yes — Redwood can emit traces and export to tracing backends; we also have a webhooks stream for metrics ingestion into Datadog. The Console includes token-level cost and route dashboards.
[03:20] Priya: For the Private option, what's the typical networking pattern? VPC peering? Transit?
[03:25] Maya: For Private we offer two modes — VPC peering into our private control plane, or an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. Peering is the most common: you set up VPC/VPN and we exchange routes, support private endpoints. We'll need one of your network engineers for a deep-dive.
[03:41] Marco: Latency-wise, peering is acceptable. Our main worry is data residency — some customers require data never leave region.
[03:48] Maya: We have region pinning for model serving and can do private-only deployments that keep data in-region. We'll add details in the security doc.
[03:56] Luis: About KMS — can we require that customer-managed keys encrypt logs and token payloads?
[04:02] Jules: For Private/Dedicated we support CMK for model request payload encryption at rest and offer integration patterns for HSM-backed KMS. For Hosted we use Redwood-managed keys by default but support Bring Your Own Key on enterprise plans.
[04:18] Elena: Great. Pricing — rough numbers? We want a ballpark for Dedicated.
[04:22] Maya: We'll give ballpark ranges based on committed qps/throughput. I'll follow up with a tiered estimate: baseline committed + burst pool add-on. That'll come in the email.
[04:33] Marco: Is there an eval path? We want to run a small POC for 2 weeks with our retrieval pipeline and the LangChain flows.
[04:39] Maya: Absolutely. Typical POC is 2-4 weeks: we provide credits on Hosted or spin up a small Dedicated pool depending on your needs. For RAG workloads it's useful to test prefix/KV caching behavior — that can drop token cost significantly.
[04:53] Aaron: How does caching interact with LlamaIndex? We're doing a lot of retrieval-heavy prompts.
[04:58] Jules: We expose prefix caching and KV cache. For RAG you can cache completions or precompute embeddings at ingestion. LlamaIndex connectors can be configured to hit cached embeddings. We'll include guidance in the example repo.
[05:12] Marco: Any gotchas around LangChain's Retriever interface?
[05:15] Jules: Only mismatch is if LangChain expects streaming tokens in a particular chunk size. Our streaming api is configurable; you'll probably need a small adapter but we've open-sourced adapters for common versions.
[05:28] Elena: On quotas — we have multiple product tiers; each tenant needs its own quota and rate limit. Can Redwood support per-API-key quotas?
[05:36] Maya: Yes — per-api-key and per-route quota enforcement is supported. You can also enforce per-customer plans via an internal gateway which maps to different api-keys.
[05:45] Priya: How do we handle schema changes if we switch models mid-rollout?
[05:49] Jules: Redwood has rollout controls and model version pinning so you can canary traffic to new model versions. If schema (structured output) changes, the evals system can run prompt tests and detect regressions automatically.
[06:02] Marco: We use internal metrics to calculate unit economics. Is there a token cost API we can poll?
[06:07] Ravi: There's a usage API that returns token counts + cost per call. We also stream per-request events to your observability pipeline.
[06:16] Luis: Logging and PI — do you redact PII automatically? We need controls to avoid storing raw user text in logs.
[06:24] Jules: By default, logs can be configured to exclude request text; audit logs include metadata only. For Private we can disable request retention entirely. We'll document retention policies.
[06:36] Elena: Ok, so immediate asks from us: 1) SOC2 + KMS docs, 2) LangChain/LlamaIndex sample and perf script, 3) Dedicated pricing, 4) network deep-dive. Right?
[06:46] Maya: Correct. I'll send a recap email after this call.
[06:50] Marco: One subtle point — we may have an internal gateway already doing auth and rate limiting; would you consider an "adapter" pattern where our gateway proxies to Redwood but also rewrites headers for cost attribution?
[07:00] Jules: Yep that's common — gateway can attach a customer header and Redwood will honor it for billing/attribution. If you need server-side adapter code we can provide a lightweight proxy example in node/go.
[07:14] Aaron: On monitoring, does Redwood support spike detection alerts? We want anomaly alerts.
[07:18] Ravi: We emit metrics you can hook into Datadog and set alerts on p95/p99 token rates and error rates; Redwood Console also supports alerting on regression.
[07:30] Elena: Any blockers from a legal/procurement perspective — standard SLA acceptable?
[07:35] Maya: Our enterprise SLAs are negotiable for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we have standard up-time terms. If procurement needs specific contract language we'll route to our legal.
[07:46] Priya: Timeline? We are aiming to have a supplier decision by end of September. POC in early September ideally.
[07:53] Maya: That's doable. We'll aim to have the docs and pricing in a follow-up this week to start POC early next week.
[08:01] Elena: Cool. Quick technical clarifying question from Marco — does Redwood support per-request metadata propagation so we can tie model responses to our trace IDs?
[08:09] Jules: Yes pass-through of trace headers like X-Trace-ID is supported, and we will include them in logs and outgoing traces.
[08:18] Marco: One more — if we set up a Dedicated pool, what's the expected lead time?
[08:23] Maya: Small Dedicated pools can be provisioned in 3-5 business days; larger committed pools take longer. For POC we often use Hosted credits or a tiny Dedicated with burst.
[08:34] Luis: For compliance, can audit logs be exported to our S3 with SSE-KMS?
[08:40] Jules: Yes — logs export to customer S3 buckets with server-side encryption and optional KMS.
[08:46] Elena: Perfect. Anything else from Redwood?
[08:49] Maya: Just that we'll send the example repo, security pack, and pricing. Also propose Aug 25 10:00 UTC for technical deep-dive — is that ok?
[08:59] Marco: Works for me.
[09:01] Priya: Works.
[09:03] Luis: Fine.
[09:04] Maya: Great. Recap of next steps and action items — see email. Thanks everyone.
[09:12] Elena: Thanks all, appreciate it.
[09:15] (meeting ends)

Note: transcription contains minor speaker label errors and occasional filler words, e.g., "um" trimmed. Some product names may be lightly mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash in one note).
